extracted.intended_audience: scholars of journalism/media studies, journalists, newsroom managers, and media reformers interested in racial disparities in local news selection
extracted.subtask_description: Framework and empirical criteria for diagnosing why local television news systematically under-covers communities of color; identifies mechanisms, operational selection criteria, measurable metrics, and reform implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incognizant Racism
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworkers' systematic failure to perceive minority-community stories as newsworthy, deriving not from explicit intent but from routinized application of professional news values and background assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core concept: the routinized application of 'neutral' news values by predominantly white, middle-class decision-makers produces selection patterns that miss or distort coverage of communities of color. Use this as the explanatory lens when evaluating selection decisions rather than attributing disparities solely to explicit prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: News-Value Calibration to Majority Audience
rubrics_metrics.description: "Universal" news values are calibrated against majority-audience interests; events relevant to minority communities consistently fail the threshold for selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether stated news values implicitly assume a white, middle-class imagined viewer; check if stories germane to minority audiences are judged less newsworthy because they don't match that imagined-audience profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source-Network Whiteness
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters' established source networks are predominantly white, professional, and institutional; minority-community sources require enterprise reporting to locate and cultivate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whose voices are in the routine 'rolodex' and whether relying on existing networks privileges institutional/white sources. Consider the additional labor required to develop community sources as a practical barrier to selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat Geography
rubrics_metrics.description: News beats are anchored in white-majority areas (e.g., city hall, downtown, business districts); minority neighborhoods are often covered only via crime beats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine newsroom beat assignments and whether geographical coverage structurally omits everyday civic, cultural, and economic life in minority neighborhoods by confining coverage to crime-related beats.

rubrics_metrics.name: "White" Content Delivered by Diverse Anchors
rubrics_metrics.description: Visible newsroom diversity at the anchor level can mask white-dominated decision-making about which stories run and how they are framed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate on-air diversity with diversity in editorial power; evaluate who controls story selection and framing, not just who appears on screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative-Frame Default
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of minority communities is concentrated in negative frames—crime, accidents, deficits—while community successes, leadership, and civic engagement are under-covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for systematic framing patterns; count positive vs. negative frames applied to minority communities and compare to coverage of white communities to detect default negative framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place-Branding Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated negative coverage of specific neighborhoods (always associated with crime stories) reinforces audience perceptions of those areas as unsafe, creating a feedback loop with real consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace how recurring story selection about particular places shapes place-branding and then in turn influences future selection decisions; consider long-term reinforcement effects when auditing coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-Demographic Match (Operational Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Story selection is optimized for the imagined-typical-viewer (often a white middle-class suburbanite); perceived audience demographics drive what is considered newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing selection choices, identify the imagined audience being optimized for and whether that model excludes or downgrades stories relevant to other demographic groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiar-Source Premium (Operational Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories with sources already in reporters' or editors' rolodexes outpace stories that require new source-finding labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure or note the advantage afforded to stories that can be produced quickly using established institutional sources versus the additional time and effort needed to cultivate community sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictable-Frame Compatibility (Operational Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that fit established narrative frames (e.g., crime, tragedy, community) are easier to compose and thus more likely to be selected; minority-community stories often require novel frames and thus face higher barriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how much selection favors stories that slot into familiar frames and whether editors penalize stories that require creative framing or additional context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual-Compatibility Bias (Operational Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsroom assumptions about what looks "right" for general-audience TV news skew against unfamiliar communities and settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess visual norms that influence selection (what 'looks good' on TV) and whether these norms systematically exclude or misrepresent minority-community spaces and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed of Source Verification (Operational Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Established institutional sources verify quickly; community sources often require more time to verify, disadvantaging stories that depend on them in fast news cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider time-to-verify as a pragmatic gatekeeper: fast-verifying sources are privileged in tight production schedules. Audit editorial workflows to see how verification speed influences selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crime-Heavy Coverage (Empirical Finding / Metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Black and Latino subjects appear disproportionately in crime stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use content analysis to quantify subject distribution across story types; disproportionate representation of minority subjects in crime pieces is evidence of biased selection and framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtering Out of Successful Minority-Community Stories (Empirical Finding / Metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Positive minority-community events (community organizations, business openings, cultural events) are frequently pitched but rarely selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track pitches vs. selected stories to measure what positive community reporting is being lost. Compare acceptance rates for minority-community positive stories to those for majority-community ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor Decisions Based on "Audience Interest" Heuristics (Empirical Finding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors invoke imagined-audience preferences to justify excluding minority-community stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating editorial rationales, flag appeals to vague 'audience interest' as a heuristic that may mask structural biases; require evidence linking audience data to selection choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporters-of-Color Frustration and Barrier (Empirical Finding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Minority reporters often struggle to get minority-community stories accepted, even when stories are professionally well-developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document experiences of reporters of color regarding pitch acceptance and editorial feedback; use such testimonial and process data as indicators of structural obstruction rather than individual failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural Racial Bias Prediction (Implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying newsworthiness criteria 'neutrally' predicts systematic race-disparate coverage; structural features of routines produce disparate outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structural analysis (not solely individual intent) to explain and predict coverage disparities; test whether neutral application of existing criteria correlates with race-disparate outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage Parity Ratios as an Operational Metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage parity ratios compare minority-community story counts to demographic share and can be measured and benchmarked across outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalize parity: compute ratios of minority-related stories (and positive vs. negative frames) relative to population or civic-activity baselines; use these metrics for audits, accountability, and cross-outlet comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsroom Diversity (Reform Recommendation / Criterion for Improvement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Increasing racial diversity in newsrooms is recommended to change background assumptions and decision-making processes that produce incognizant racism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate diversity not only by hiring but by decision-making authority, beat assignments, and inclusion in source-network building; measure whether increased diversity changes selection patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source-Network Diversification (Reform Recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberate diversification of source networks to include community leaders and non-institutional voices is necessary to broaden story selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess newsroom efforts to cultivate and maintain community sources; create metrics for source diversity (e.g., proportion of stories relying on community vs. institutional sources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat Reorganization (Reform Recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reorganizing beats so that coverage is not territorially or institutionally anchored in white-majority areas can expand routine attention to minority neighborhoods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit beat maps and reassign beats to ensure routine coverage of civic life in minority neighborhoods, not only crime; track resulting changes in story topics and frames.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Audit Metrics and Accountability (Reform Recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementing audit metrics (e.g., parity ratios, source-diversity measures, beat-coverage maps) allows monitoring and intervention to reduce disparate coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend regular public reporting of coverage audits, incorporation of parity benchmarks in editorial reviews, and use of quantitative and qualitative measures to evaluate reform progress.
